sources.design: Guideline based on systematic review; nonoperative advice best-practice opinion
sources.population: Adults with native GHOA and anatomic TSA; not reverse/revision arthroplasty or primary RA.
sources.comparator: No high/moderate-quality nonoperative comparative PT study; postoperative comparisons separate.
sources.outcomes: PT may benefit selected patients; no specific intervention superiority established.
sources.followUp: Underlying cohort through three years; varied surgical follow-up.
sources.uncertainty: Insufficient comparative evidence; clinical expertise supports individualization.
sources.harms: Intensity mismatched to irritability may increase pain; no per-exercise harm threshold.
sources.limitations: Hip/knee OA or postoperative data cannot supply native-shoulder exercise efficacy.

protocol.execution: Select ROM/strength exercises for individual impairments and irritability, not a fixed program.
protocol.dose: not reported as optimal universal dose.
protocol.frequency: not reported as optimal universal frequency.
protocol.progression: Individual response-guided, not a validated fixed progression.
protocol.stoppingRules: Increased pain possible if intensity mismatched; no numeric stopping rule.

sources.limitations: No exact exercises/dose or general safety clearance.

protocol.execution: reported in accessible text: Abstract: some patients received physiotherapy, rehabilitation and a shoulder strap targeting range of motion and muscle strength, alongside discretionary conventional care. Exact movements, sets and loads unreported.
protocol.supervision: reported in accessible text: Abstract: some patients received ROM/muscular-strength training from a physical therapist. No exact therapist visit schedule or universal participation reported.

sources.comparator: Patient-chosen PT versus no PT within multimodal cohort.
sources.coInterventions: Analgesics, NSAIDs and corticosteroid injections offered.
sources.outcomes: No ASES change difference with PT (P=.524); 31% met clinical improvement; 14/62 underwent TSA.
sources.harms: No detailed exercise-injury attribution; authors loading-aggravation explanation speculative.
sources.limitations: No causal conclusion strengthening harmful or no patient can benefit.

protocol.execution: Standard PT emphasizing shoulder motion and strengthening; exact individual execution not described in main text.
protocol.supervision: PT performed at location chosen by patient.
protocol.progression: After six weeks continued care or arthroplasty elected; no exercise-specific progression.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as exercise-specific numeric stop rule.

findings.statement: Guideline offers individualized ROM/strength PT as best-practice opinion; no intervention superiority or high/moderate-quality nonoperative comparisons.

citations.location: Best Practice Statements > Nonoperative Physical Therapist Services
Best Practice Statements > Nonoperative Physical Therapist Interventions

findings.statement: Older multimodal cohort improved; newer self-selected cohort did not show PT-associated ASES benefit.
findings.limitations: No randomized causal comparison; loading harm speculation not a contraindication.

gaps: Insufficient evidence for a condition-specific exact exercise mapping, load/ROM threshold or blanket exclusion; mappings/rules withheld.
No exact candidate exercise extracted; underlying Guo protocol unavailable and Su main-text variants unspecified.
No therapeutic release; independent clinical review needed.
